newsitem.title: UK: "Loyalist" inmates end N.Ireland prison dispute.
newsitem.headline: "Loyalist" inmates end N.Ireland prison dispute.

text.p: Convicted pro-British guerrillas ended a tense three-day dispute about new security measures at Northern Ireland's main prison near Belfast on Friday, a leading Protestant politician said.

"They are pleased that their concerns have been addressed and I am pleased that we have been able to negotiate a settlement of this," Ulster Democratic Party leader Gary McMichael said after meeting the inmates.

Prison authorities had adopted "a common sense approach" and the men had also compromised, he said. "It is a great step forward to be able to resolve this without any further confrontation," he told BBC television.

The Loyalist prisoners had tried to burn down two watchtowers and had climbed on to cellblock rooftops in a protest against security measures brought in as a result of a foiled tunnel escape attempt last month by Irish Republican Army prisoners.
Called Loyalist because they want British rule to continue, they said they were being unfairly punished for IRA wrongdoing.

McMichael, whose group has political links with the banned Ulster Defence Association and Ulster Freedom Fighters, denied media reports that hoax bomb alerts that caused traffic chaos in Belfast were the work of supporters of the prisoners.
"There's nothing to suggest that it was tied to this dispute," he said.
